propositions.text: The appellant is Mr. Hamid Alakozai who appeals the Federal Court's dismissal of his judicial review application.
propositions.quote: The appellant, Mr. Hamid Alakozai, appeals from a decision of the Federal Court dated May 1, 2019, dismissing his application for judicial review

propositions.text: The Federal Court found the RCMP's denial of the appellant's Enhanced Reliability Status application reasonable.
propositions.quote: on the basis of its finding that the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s (RCMP) decision to deny the appellant’s application for an Enhanced Reliability Status was reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, Mr. Hamid Alakozai, appeals the Federal Court's dismissal of his judicial review application regarding the RCMP's denial of his Enhanced Reliability Status.

propositions.text: The appellant is a dual citizen of Canada and Afghanistan, employed with the Corps of Commissionaires, holding Secret security clearance.
propositions.quote: The appellant, a dual citizen of Canada and Afghanistan, is presently employed with the Corps of Commissionaires and holds a Secret security clearance

propositions.text: In September 2015, the appellant applied to become a Regular Member of the RCMP requiring Top Secret clearance and Enhanced Reliability Status.
propositions.quote: In September 2015, the appellant submitted an application to become a Regular Member of the RCMP. As a prerequisite to employment as a Regular Member, which requires Top Secret security clearance, it was necessary for the appellant to obtain an Enhanced Reliability Status

propositions.text: The RCMP began an internal security screening including polygraph, interview, and assessment of identity, qualifications, honesty, and loyalty.
propositions.quote: the RCMP began its internal security screening process. The process required the appellant to undergo a Pre-Employment Polygraph and security interview and to be assessed by an RCMP Risk Investigator to verify his identity, his education and professional qualifications, and his honesty and loyalty

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a dual citizen employed with the Corps of Commissionaires, applied to the RCMP requiring Enhanced Reliability Status and underwent security screening.

propositions.text: The RCMP screening revealed concerns about the appellant's online presence and social media accounts.
propositions.quote: The RCMP’s screening process revealed a number of concerns with the appellant, particularly with respect to his online presence and social media accounts

propositions.text: Concerns included appellant's self-representations as an Ambassador, doctor, legal advisor, consultant, and political party leader.
propositions.quote: These concerns were documented in the Continuation Report... They included the appellant’s representations of himself as, among other things, an “Ambassador of Humanity”, a doctor, a senior legal advisor, an international legal and political consultant, and the leader of the National Uprising Party of Afghanistan

paragraphs.summary: The RCMP screening found concerns about the appellant's online presence, including self-representations as various prominent roles.

propositions.text: The Continuation Report noted appellant's appearances in YouTube videos and over 2,000 Facebook friends, including one linked to an extremist group.
propositions.quote: The Continuation Report also highlighted the appellant’s appearances in a variety of YouTube videos... The Continuation Report further found that the appellant had over 2,000 Facebook friends, one of whom national security experts identified as likely belonging to an extremist group

paragraphs.summary: The Continuation Report noted appellant's YouTube appearances and Facebook friends, including one linked to extremism.

propositions.text: The Risk Investigator gave the appellant a follow-up interview to explain concerns.
propositions.quote: The Risk Investigator decided to provide the appellant with a follow-up interview to allow the appellant the opportunity to provide explanations

propositions.text: In the second interview, appellant attributed misrepresentations to cultural and language differences and said his wife managed his Facebook account.
propositions.quote: During this interview, the appellant attributed the misrepresentations to differences in culture and language use... his wife had access to his account and may have accepted friend requests indiscriminately

propositions.text: Appellant stated he was no longer involved in Afghan politics, was cleaning up Facebook, and discussed friend request scrutiny with his wife.
propositions.quote: he was no longer involved in the Afghan political party he had founded... He indicated that he was cleaning up his Facebook account and had discussed the importance of scrutinizing friend requests with his wife

paragraphs.summary: The appellant explained misrepresentations as cultural differences and said he was cleaning up Facebook after a follow-up interview.

propositions.text: Two months after the second interview, re-examination found no corrections and more concerning Facebook friends.
propositions.quote: The re-examination found that the appellant had not corrected any of the misrepresentations nor deleted the problematic Facebook contact, and had in fact acquired more concerning Facebook friends

propositions.text: A further re-examination on March 22, 2018, showed appellant still had not corrected misrepresentations.
propositions.quote: A further re-examination conducted on March 22, 2018 indicated that the appellant had still not corrected the misrepresentations

paragraphs.summary: Re-examinations found appellant did not correct misrepresentations and gained more concerning Facebook friends.

propositions.text: The Risk Investigator recommended denial of Enhanced Reliability Status based on political ambitions, family security concerns, misrepresentations, extremist contacts, and poor judgment.
propositions.quote: the Risk Investigator recommended that the appellant’s application for an Enhanced Reliability Status be denied... based on the appellant’s apparent Afghan political ambitions, security concerns relating to the appellant’s family in Afghanistan, the numerous inaccuracies and misrepresentations on the appellant’s social media accounts, his acceptance of Facebook friends appearing to participate in violent extremism, and his failure to take remedial action

paragraphs.summary: The Risk Investigator recommended denial due to political ambitions, family security concerns, misrepresentations, extremist contacts, and poor judgment.

propositions.text: On June 4, 2018, the RCMP Director denied the appellant's Enhanced Reliability Status application citing security concerns and dishonesty.
propositions.quote: the Director had denied his application for an Enhanced Reliability Status on the basis of the appellant’s involvement in behaviours and activities with security or reliability implications... and a lack of honesty in providing evasive, misleading, or false information

propositions.text: The appellant sought judicial review of the denial decision.
propositions.quote: The appellant sought judicial review of the denial decision

paragraphs.summary: The RCMP Director denied the appellant's application for security concerns and dishonesty; appellant sought judicial review.

propositions.text: The Federal Court determined the applicable standard of review was reasonableness.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court determined that the applicable standard of review was reasonableness

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court determined the standard of review was reasonableness.

propositions.text: The TBS Standard grants deputy heads discretion to determine security screening requirements.
propositions.quote: the TBS Standard grants deputy heads of all departments the discretion to determine department-specific security screening requirements

propositions.text: RCMP officials assess trustworthiness of applicants per internal policies.
propositions.quote: it is the responsibility of RCMP officials to assess the trustworthiness of applicants for RCMP positions in accordance with the RCMP’s internal policies

propositions.text: The appellant was afforded procedural fairness and opportunity to respond and amend social media accounts.
propositions.quote: the appellant was afforded procedural fairness throughout the process, and was given the opportunity to respond to the Risk Investigator’s concerns in a second interview and to make changes to the problematic social media accounts

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court found deputy heads have discretion, RCMP assesses trustworthiness, and appellant had procedural fairness.

propositions.text: The Director had strong evidence to deny Enhanced Reliability Status and the decision was reasonable.
propositions.quote: the Director had sufficiently strong evidence to conclude that the appellant should be denied an Enhanced Reliability Status and that the decision was therefore reasonable

propositions.text: The Federal Court dismissed the judicial review application.
propositions.quote: It accordingly dismissed the application for judicial review

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court found the denial reasonable and dismissed the judicial review application.

propositions.text: The issue on appeal is whether the Federal Court chose and applied the correct standard of review.
propositions.quote: The issue on appeal is whether the Federal Court chose the correct standard of review and applied it properly

paragraphs.summary: The issue is whether the Federal Court chose and applied the correct standard of review.

propositions.text: The Federal Court's role is not to re-weigh evidence but to determine if the Director's decision was reasonable.
propositions.quote: The role of the Federal Court on judicial review is not to re-weigh the evidence. Rather, it is to determine whether the Director’s decision was reasonable given the evidence before him

propositions.text: This Court on appeal considers if the Federal Court identified and applied the correct standard of review.
propositions.quote: Similarly, this Court on appeal is restricted to considering whether the Federal Court identified the correct standard of review and applied it properly

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court must determine reasonableness; this Court reviews if the Federal Court applied the correct standard.

propositions.text: The Federal Court correctly identified reasonableness as the standard of review for security status decisions.
propositions.quote: the Federal Court correctly identified the standard of review for decisions relating to security status as reasonableness

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires decisions to be transparent, justified, intelligible, and within acceptable outcomes (Dunsmuir).
propositions.quote: A reasonable decision must be transparent, justified, and intelligible, and must fall within the range of acceptable outcomes on the facts and law (Dunsmuir v. New Brunswick, 2008 SCC 9 at para. 47)

propositions.text: The Federal Court properly applied the reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court also properly applied the standard of review

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court correctly identified and properly applied the reasonableness standard of review.

propositions.text: The appellant's loyalty to Canada was not at issue and did not inform the Director's decision.
propositions.quote: The appellant’s loyalty to Canada... is not at issue in this proceeding and did not inform the Director’s decision

propositions.text: The decision was based on appellant's involvement in behaviors with security or reliability implications.
propositions.quote: the decision was based on the appellant’s involvement in behaviours and activities with security or reliability implications

propositions.text: Two examples justified the decision: association with individuals involved in criminal activities and lack of honesty during security process.
propositions.quote: The letter highlighted two examples... association, affiliation, or contact with individuals who have been involved in criminal activities... lack of honesty in providing evasive, misleading, or false information

propositions.text: These grounds provide sufficient justification; the decision was transparent and intelligible.
propositions.quote: these grounds constitute sufficient justification for the decision. Furthermore, in my opinion the decision was also transparent and intelligible

paragraphs.summary: The decision was justified by appellant's associations and dishonesty, and was transparent and intelligible.

propositions.text: There was ample evidence to support denial including political ambitions and family security concerns.
propositions.quote: there was ample evidence before the RCMP to support a denial... including... appellant’s apparent Afghan political ambitions and security concerns relating to his family members in Afghanistan

propositions.text: No error in the Federal Court's application of the standard of review was found.
propositions.quote: I therefore see no error in the Federal Court’s application of the standard of review

paragraphs.summary: Ample evidence supported denial; no error found in Federal Court's application of standard of review.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed without costs.
propositions.quote: I would dismiss the appeal without costs

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is dismissed without costs.
